item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption explains how people can be manipulated into participating in corruption.
item.support: provides insights into how individuals can, contrary to their initial instincts, be drawn into a corrupt scheme.

item.text: It uses investigation examples and case studies to examine coercion, compromise and grooming, including manipulation between public officials.
item.support: Drawing on examples from its own investigations and case studies from other bodies

item.text: The Commission reports that detailed plans to groom officials over long periods are unusual in its experience.
item.support: it is unusual to see evidence of detailed, long-term plans to target and groom a public official.

item.text: The Commission advises agencies to disrupt potentially improper relationships through measures such as staff rotation, shared responsibilities and team assignments.
item.support: a useful anti-corruption technique is to disrupt the potential for improper relationships to form between insiders and outsiders.

item.quote: Consequently, a checklist of warning signs may not provide much protection against a skilled, determined manipulator.
